chapter: Arriving in New York and founding the Afro-Cubans
title: Approaching the Park Plaza: Montecino's guerrilla jibe
summary: Machito asked the Park Plaza owner for a date and Montecino, whose dance was postponed, sneered at his guerrilla.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay. Now, how long after that rehearsal did you start getting work?
I mean - - after that rehearsal, it was about a month or two months.

So Mario tell me: "Macho, the band is ready", so I went to the Park Plaza and - lucky, one of those lucky moments - I went to the Park Plaza, Montecino happened to be the leader, he had a - there was postponed one of the dance on Saturday. That was a Monday, so I went up there because I was a regular player for a band, and asked the owner that I have a band and the guy paid me no attention, so in that particular moment Montecino came and said: "Hey, Macho - hello, how are you? How is your guerrilla? you know, he ahh you know, and minor things. Yeah, well you know, Mmmnn - so on , so on ......
When you say - when they were saying guerrilla, what exactly does that mean?
A second, a third-rate ahh like you say guerrilla, you don't consider this an army.......
....it's a bunch of guys with a gun or machine gun or whatever, you understand?
.....that's why he called me a guerrilla. How is your guerrilla? Well ......
I know what I had. He didn't offend me.
